channel.title: Doc Radar
channel.description: Upcoming documentary releases from the distributors, broadcasters, streamers and sales agents that matter. Updated weekly.

item.title: The Last First: Winter K2 (Apple Original Films)
item.description: Directed by Amir Bar-Lev. A historic race to become the first to summit K2 in winter unravels into tragedy, exposing how ambition, ego, and the pursuit of glory can be as dangerous as the mountain itself.

item.title: Africa Earth's Wild Home
item.description: African wildlife and landscapes is brought to the screen like never before, using the latest technology to tell the most extraordinary stories from the continent and cutting-edge CGI to unearth the deep history and forces that shaped Africa's natural worlds.

item.title: Try!
item.description: Directed by Oisín Mistéil. Four Irish Rugby teams who defy stereotypes tackle their way to the Mixed Ability Rugby World Cup, where full-contact sport meets joyful belonging.

item.title: Kikuyu Land
item.description: Directed by Andrew H. Brown. As a Nairobi journalist probes a land battle entangling the local government and a powerful multinational corporation, covered wounds are revealed and family secrets are exposed.

item.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
item.description: Directed by Alex Gibney. In 2022, Salman Rushdie was preparing to deliver a lecture on the United States as a safe haven for writers when a man rushed the stage and, in 27 seconds, stabbed him 15 times. Airlifted to hospital, Rushdie survived, barely, and his wife Rachel Eliza Griffiths began filming immediately, capturing an unfiltered view of his recovery, return to life and how he regained his spirit and hope for the future.

item.title: Secrets of the Southwest: Science Behind the Secrets
item.description: Meet the inspiring individuals and communities who work to protect our most beloved UK wildlife.

item.title: Secrets of the Southwest
item.description: Discover the hidden stories Britain's southwest has to offer. From Foxes fighting on the streets of Bristol to Puffins looking for love on Skomer Island.

item.title: Woven Ground
item.description: Directed by Blair Coron. Composer Blair Coron takes his musical instruments, recording equipment and friends to the islands, glens and forests of Scotland to record directly in the landscapes that inspired the music.

item.title: Schumacher '94 - The Birth of a Legend (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Christin Freitag. Michael Schumacher's first World Championship win roars to life through personal interviews and archival footage of the legendary 1994 Formula 1 season.

item.title: Garden Sanctuary
item.description: Directed by Jovial H. FIsh. My Walk on the 2nd of October.

item.title: Travel Reminiscence
item.description: Directed by Barney Gibbons. At a London community centre, facilitators and volunteers run a travel-themed session for people living with dementia and their families, friends and carers. Together, the group embarks on a playful journey: discussing past trips, revisiting these through theatre, and writing postcards to loved ones.

item.title: The Dance of the Kokorrdit
item.description: Directed by Elio B Cunampio. A Wounaan teenager and a leader of their community venture into the Darién in search of a sacred bird. Along the way, they will face the dangers that threaten their territory and their culture.

item.title: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger
item.description: Directed by Dylan Southern. Experience the meteoric rise of Oasis through rare footage and untold stories as the band reunites for Oasis Live '25, chronicling their journey from Manchester streets to global rock stardom.

item.title: André Leon Talley — Style is Forever (Greenwich Entertainment)
item.description: Directed by Zach Stafford. André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

item.title: Lesbian Lines
item.description: Directed by Cara Holmes. In a silenced Ireland, a community of lesbians builds an underground network of helplines - offering connection, survival, and defiance through the simple act of answering the phone.

item.title: Everest: The Other Side (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Jimmy Chin. An intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible. Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Mount Everest—the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on Earth—something only a handful have ever achieved, and no one has successfully skied down.

item.title: Always Lalisa
item.description: Directed by Sue Kim. Documentary following global superstar LISA during a transformative year away from BLACKPINK, the K-pop phenomenon that made her one of the world's most recognizable performers. Documenting a year of risk, reinvention, and self-discovery as LISA begins to define her next chapter.

item.title: Transformation
item.description: Directed by Ganna Tretiak. A feature-length documentary exploring the profound inner metamorphosis of Ukrainian civilians from the creative sector who chose to enlist as soldiers to defend their country. The film maps the deep psychological and lifestyle shifts experienced by musicians, artists, and filmmakers as they stepped away from civilian art to enter the realities of war.

item.title: Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Nanette Burstein. Serving as an intimate and cinematic portrait of Sagan, the Untitled Carl Sagan Documentary will explore his love story with partner Ann Druyan and with science. The film will include exclusive audio recordings, archival clips and animation, along with interviews with his family, friends and colleagues. With the full support of Sagan’s family and friends, the film will present a fascinating look into the life and career of one of the world’s most inspiring and revolutionizing scientists of our time.

item.title: Lady Liberty: Secrets of an Icon (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Julien Johan. This iconic statue was a gift from France to the new-born American Republic and was the first crowd-funded monument of all time. A symbol of emancipation and freedom, which took two decades to be completed. The film features original 3D virtual reconstitutions of Auguste Bartholdi’s Atelier in Paris and travels back in time to bring viewers at the heart of the Statue’s original construction, revealing the founding ideals of our democracies.

item.title: NAZA
item.description: Directed by Yuval Abraham. In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

item.title: Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald
item.description: Directed by Judd Apatow. Built entirely from archival footage, personal photos, and rare home videos contributed by fans and friends, Norm tell his own story in his own voice.

item.title: Duckweed
item.description: Directed by Matthew Berka. Obscure, aging, and living on the outskirts of London, writer of supernatural fiction Quentin Crisp asks himself a fundamental existential question: ‘Who am I?' This feature-length film-essay is structured around readings of Crisp’s own zuihitsu of the same name, which, in essence, is the story of his life. As we follow Crisp on a walk deeper into the ‘‘little wood’’ of his private landscape, the binaries of success and failure begin to fade away.

item.title: Enter the Television
item.description: Directed by Thomas Edward Seymour. From Tom Seymour creator of the VHS Massacre Trilogy. Enter the Television is a feature-length documentary exploring the dark corners of television from obscure commercials to unconventional cable programming. It examines the evolution of media through an underground lens, revealing how independent voices survive within systems controlled by powerful media corporations.

item.title: Forza on the Run
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 02: The French police have put the illegal drift racers of Paris on final notice, so they've took off on the run across the border into Belgium. Hanrahan rides along with the crew as they dodge police and takeover Brussels.

item.title: TOMORROW X TOGETHER WORLD TOUR 'ACT:TOMORROW'
item.description: Directed by Taehwan Yum. ACT:TOMORROW is the fourth world tour by TOMORROW X TOGETHER. The tour commenced on August 22, 2025 in Seoul, South Korea.

item.title: Back to the Beginning: Ozzy's Final Bow
item.description: Directed by Ben Wainwright-Pearce. A powerful return to roots, this concert captures Black Sabbath in peak form - reuniting to deliver classic hits with raw energy and legendary precision.

item.title: All About the Money
item.description: Directed by Sinéad O'Shea. A son of one of America’s wealthiest families creates a communist revolutionary base in rural Massachusetts as a means of disrupting the capitalist system he grew up in, but has now come to despise. It’s the starting point of an astonishing journey.

item.title: Nuisance Bear
item.description: Directed by Gabriela Osio Vanden. A polar bear is forced to navigate a human world of tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as its ancient migration collides with modern life. When a sacred predator is branded a nuisance, it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

item.title: Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down
item.description: Directed by Christoph Farwig. "Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down" is a documentary film about British social policy. The focus is on the political struggle against neoliberal austerity policies, which have their origins in the hated Thatcher government. The film features the former socialist MP Dave Nellist, who is now the national chair of the Trade Unionist & Socialist Coalition and Hannah Sell, the general secretary of the Socialist Party. The film features a local election campaign in the miners' town of Nuneaton, students campaigning against an increase in tuition fees and refuse workers from Birmingham striking against massive cuts to their wages.

item.title: Beyond
item.description: Directed by Ben Menashe. Beyond follows people living with and beyond cancer as they discover strength, connection, and a new sense of possibility through climbing. Set between indoor walls and wild mountain rock, it is a powerful story about recovery becoming adventure.

item.title: George Michael: The Faith Tour
item.description: Directed by Andy Morahan. A stunning delve into George Michael's 1988 Faith Tour, as shot live at the famous Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy. This exclusive footage, assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm over two nights (30–31 May 1988), features the 24-year-old pop star at the height of his powers.

item.title: Making Marie Antoinette
item.description: Directed by Eleanor Coppola. Eleanor Coppola's behind-the-scenes documentation of her daughter Sofia Coppola directing the 2006 film Marie Antoinette, capturing the craftsmanship and challenges of being a young female director.

item.title: Finding Faith
item.description: Directed by Mary McCartney. A short film contextualising the cultural significance of George Michael's Faith Tour via unheard interview voice-over, unseen images by Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

item.title: 1 in 2
item.description: Directed by David Wilkinson. Nearly one in two of us will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in our lives. David Nicholas Wilkinson is one of them, twice over. 1 in 2 follows Wilkinson through his own treatment, where he discovers a steep rise in bowel cancer among people far too young to be screened for it, and far too young, it seems, to be believed.

item.title: Whiddy (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Adrian McCarthy. A small rural community in Ireland welcomes in a major, global oil company with open arms but just 10 years and numerous oil spills later, that dream turns into an unimaginable nightmare. 50 lives lost in a tragedy that silenced and divided the community and still haunts it to this day.

item.title: The Neighbourhood is Changing
item.description: Documentary on the making and legacy of Mulberry Street featuring new interviews with cast and crew

item.title: American Doctor
item.description: Directed by Poh Si Teng. United by a shared oath to save lives, three American doctors—Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—work in a besieged hospital in Gaza and return to the United States to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind.

item.title: Phantom 814
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 03: Unique access to the most mysterious organisation in France. Jake Hanrahan travels with the bizarre syndicate known as "814SSR". They shoot guns, host fight clubs, and make money in the underground. Yet still, they insist they're not a gang and are simply doing hardcore trolling. The truth? Decide for yourself...

item.title: Remember the Summit
item.description: Directed by Timothy Dhalleine. Sir Chris Bonington’s return to Torres del Paine, 62 years after the first ascent of the Central Tower. At 91 years old, and while living with Alzheimer’s disease, the documentary accompanies Bonington in a profoundly human return: an attempt to reconnect with memories that time has erased, but that the Patagonian landscape still seems to guard. During the filming, Chris once again set foot on the territory of Estancia Cerro Guido, closing a circle between past and present, between the epic of mountaineering and the fragility of memory.

item.title: Each Day in a Moment: 2026
item.description: Directed by Sam O. Burgess. One person’s perspective of the year 2026 shown through an accumulation of 365 unedited shots.

item.title: Renoir & Love
item.description: Directed by Ali Ray. Pierre-Auguste Renoir is one of the world’s favourite artists, a founding member of the Impressionist movement and a constantly evolving artist. With exclusive access to the National Gallery’s new exciting show of the same name (3 October 2026 – 31 January 2027), Exhibition on Screen will bring Renoir’s world class works to cinema audiences. Be transported back to a Parisian summer of love through the eyes of a true visionary. An unmissable opportunity to fall in love with Renoir this winter.
